findings.rationale: Local performance is far below the federation: AUC 0.564 (flagged auc z=-7.8), with CITL -0.237 and prevalence 0.360 against a mean predicted risk of 0.123, and ECE 0.245. The observed/expected ratio is inflated in both sex groups and in several income groups, which points to inflated outcome labels rather than subgroup-specific under-diagnosis. Its uploaded updates are anomalous across rounds: mean cosine to the median update is -0.83 and median norm ratio is 8.6 (flagged). Round-1 CITL is already -0.29, so the fault appears from the start.

Local AUC is 0.569 (flagged auc z=-7.7) with CITL -0.235 and prevalence 0.369 against a mean predicted risk of 0.134; ECE is 0.230 (flagged z=+19.8). Observed/expected is inflated in both sex groups, consistent with label flipping. The update stream is strongly anomalous: mean cosine -0.83, median norm ratio 6.6 (flagged). Round 1 looks clean (cosine 0.997, norm ratio 0.48), and from round 2 onward the cosine is negative with norms growing each round, so onset is round 2.

Local AUC is 0.518, essentially chance (flagged auc z=-9.2), with CITL -0.190 and prevalence 0.318 against a mean predicted risk of 0.128; ECE is 0.184 (flagged z=+14.8). Observed/expected is inflated in both sex groups and in income group 5 and 6. The updates are anomalous: mean cosine -0.78 and median norm ratio 6.4 (flagged). CITL is negative from round 4 onward and the local AUC is at chance over the whole run, so the fault is treated as present from round 1, though the round-1 signal is weaker.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed onsets with the remaining budget. Three clients (CT, UT, VT) stand apart on the same combination of signals: strongly anomalous updates (negative cosine to the median, norm ratios 6 to 9 times the median) and a collapsed local AUC (0.52 to 0.57) with prevalence about 0.32 to 0.37 against a predicted risk near 0.13. Their observed/expected ratios are inflated across sex and income subgroups, which fits flipped outcome labels (label_noise) rather than subgroup-specific under-diagnosis or a prevalence-only shift (which would leave AUC normal). I did not report VI (drift onset round 13 and a large Stroke/PhysHlth deviation), GU (weak, small-client deviations) or DC/WV/IL/SD (single feature outliers that did not persist across tools), because the evidence was within noise for small clients and the drift flags were empty. The budget is fully spent (0 left).
